title: Problem 8
statement_text: Improve the range of $|S|$ in the following theorem: for each odd prime power $q$ there is $\varepsilon_q>0$ such that if $S\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q$ with $0\in S$ and $|S|>(q+1)/2$, and $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^n$ satisfies $|A|>q^{(1-\varepsilon_q)n}$, then $A$ contains a nontrivial three-term arithmetic progression whose common difference is in $S^n$.
context_text: For a prime power $q$ and $S\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q$ with $0\in S$, a three-term arithmetic progression $x,x+d,x+2d$ in $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ has common difference in $S^n$ if every coordinate of $d$ lies in $S$; it is nontrivial if $d\neq0$. The Ellenberg–Gijswijt theorem (the cap set bound) says that a subset of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ without nontrivial three-term progressions has size at most $q^{(1-\varepsilon_q)n}$. The authors adapt Tao's slice rank method to prove: for each odd prime power $q$ there is $\varepsilon_q>0$ such that if $S\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q$, $0\in S$, $|S|>(q+1)/2$, and $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^n$ contains no nontrivial three-term arithmetic progression with common difference in $S^n$, then $|A|\le q^{(1-\varepsilon_q)n}$. For $S=\{0,1\}$, Bhangale, Khot, Liu and Minzer obtained only a density bound $O_q((\log\log\log n)^{-c_q})$ (improving density Hales–Jewett), and Green suggested that a power-saving bound might hold there. The authors say the problem already seems interesting for $|S|=\lfloor(q+1)/2\rfloor$ and, as suggested by Green, the power-saving bound may hold all the way down to $|S|=2$. This is additive combinatorics rather than graph theory.
paper_title: A note on arithmetic progressions with restricted differences

title: Problem 9
statement_text: Is there an arithmetic triangle removal lemma with restricted differences (in $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, with the differences restricted to $S^n$ for a fixed $S\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q$ containing $0$)?
context_text: For a prime power $q$ and $S\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q$ with $0\in S$, a three-term arithmetic progression $x,x+d,x+2d$ in $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ has common difference in $S^n$ if every coordinate of $d$ lies in $S$; it is nontrivial if $d\neq0$. The Ellenberg–Gijswijt theorem (the cap set bound) says that a subset of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ without nontrivial three-term progressions has size at most $q^{(1-\varepsilon_q)n}$. The authors adapt Tao's slice rank method to prove: for each odd prime power $q$ there is $\varepsilon_q>0$ such that if $S\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q$, $0\in S$, $|S|>(q+1)/2$, and $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^n$ contains no nontrivial three-term arithmetic progression with common difference in $S^n$, then $|A|\le q^{(1-\varepsilon_q)n}$. The proof goes through a multicolour sum-free theorem: if $(a_{1j},\dots,a_{dj})$, $1\le j\le N$, are $d$-tuples of elements of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ such that $a_{1j_1}+\dots+a_{dj_d}=0$ only when $j_1=\dots=j_d$, then $N\le dM(n,(q-1)n/d,q-1)$, where $M(n,D,a)$ is the number of integer solutions of $x_1+\dots+x_n\le D$ with $0\le x_i\le a$; they also prove a version with an extra polynomial constraint that handles restricted differences. The (unrestricted) multicolour sum-free result was used by Fox and Lovász, and by Fox, Lovász and Sauermann, to prove an arithmetic triangle removal lemma in $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ with polynomial bounds (Green's arithmetic triangle removal lemma states that if $X,Y,Z\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^n$ have few solutions to $x+y+z=0$, namely $o(q^{2n})$, then all solutions can be destroyed by removing $o(q^n)$ elements). The authors ask whether a restricted-differences version extending their multicolour result exists; the precise formulation is left open by the paper. This is additive combinatorics rather than graph theory.
paper_title: A note on arithmetic progressions with restricted differences
